definition.cell: phi(yes)=1, phi(unsure)=0.5, phi(no)=0. A cell is one (ruleset size K, scenario, subset seed) of a judge's shared-bank campaign, with D decoder draws. F_d is phi of the subset condition's full-set judgment in draw d; M_d is the maximum, over the subset's rules, of phi of the bank's separate-call judgment in draw d. Every call is sampled separately (a local judge's with its own seed), so F_d and M_d are independent given the scenario and rules.
definition.full_repeat: mean over the D(D-1) ordered pairs d != d' of 1[F_d != F_d']: two full-set calls disagree.
definition.identity: For independent A ~ a and B ~ b over the three labels, P(A != B) = (w_a + w_b) / 2 + ||a - b||^2 / 2 with w_a = 1 - sum_v a_v^2. With f and m a cell's distributions of F_d and M_d, repeated_draw_baseline estimates the first term, the disagreement the two calls' own draw-to-draw variability contributes, and the expected excess is the mean of ||f - m||^2 / 2 over cells: >= 0, and 0 only when every cell's two distributions coincide. Then the expected inconsistency equals the repeated-draw baseline, so does each call's expected repeat disagreement, and lenient and strict have equal expectation.
definition.inconsistency: mean over d of 1[F_d != M_d]: the ruleset-size curve's cell value.
definition.interval: A size's estimate is the mean of its cells. Every statistic's interval and sd come from one crossed scenario x subset-seed cluster bootstrap of cell means: one set of resampled scenarios and seeds, drawn as the ruleset-size curve's primary interval draws them, serves every statistic, so inconsistency's estimates and intervals are that curve's. repeated_draw_baseline, excess and lenient_minus_strict are computed from the base statistics within each replicate, and a contrast is the mean of its minuend sizes minus the mean of its subtrahend sizes within each replicate.
definition.lenient: mean over d of 1[F_d < M_d]: the full-set judgment is below the strongest single-rule judgment (no where the strongest rule says unsure or yes, or unsure where it says yes).
definition.median_inconsistency: 1[F~ != M~], with F~ the full-set judgment's median phi over the D draws (the upper median when D is even) and M~ as in rule_median_inconsistency: the full call's median judgment against the strongest rule's.
definition.null: The null f = m takes the one full-set judgment to be distributed as the maximum of the K separate-call judgments.
definition.repeated_draw_baseline: (full_repeat + separate_repeat) / 2. separate_repeat is the rate expected if the full-set judgment were one more draw of the separate-call maximum, and full_repeat the rate expected if the maximum were one more draw of the full-set judgment.
definition.rule_median_inconsistency: mean over d of 1[F_d != M~], with M~ the maximum, over the subset's rules, of each rule's median phi over the D bank draws (the upper median when D is even).
definition.separate_repeat: mean over the D(D-1) ordered pairs d != d' of 1[M_d != M_d']: two separate-call maxima disagree.
definition.strict: mean over d of 1[F_d > M_d]: the full set exceeds every rule alone.
definition.u_statistic: full_repeat and separate_repeat average over distinct draw pairs, so each is unbiased for its w.
